13.1: Arjuna asks about nature and spirit, the field and the knower of the field, knowledge and the object of knowledge.
13.2: This body is called the field; one who knows it is called the knower of the field.
13.3: Know Me as the knower of the field in all fields; knowledge of field and knower is true knowledge.
13.4: Hear briefly what the field is, its nature, modifications, origin, and who the knower is with what powers.
13.5: Sages have sung of it in many ways, in various hymns and in the reasoned verses about Brahman.
13.6: The field: the great elements, ego, intellect, the unmanifest, the ten senses, the mind and the five sense objects.
13.7: Desire, hatred, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, intelligence and firmness — these are the field with its modifications.
13.8: Knowledge begins: humility, absence of pretence, non-injury, forbearance, uprightness, service of the teacher, purity, steadfastness, self-control.
13.9: Dispassion towards sense objects, absence of ego, and reflection on the pain and evil of birth, death, old age and disease.
13.10: Non-attachment, absence of clinging to son, wife and home, and constant even-mindedness in the desirable and undesirable.
13.11: Unswerving devotion to Me, resort to solitude, and distaste for crowds.
13.12: Constancy in knowledge of the Self and insight into the goal of true knowledge — all this is declared to be knowledge; the rest is ignorance.
13.13: Now what is to be known, by knowing which one attains immortality: the beginningless supreme Brahman, said to be neither being nor non-being.
13.14: With hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads and mouths everywhere, hearing everywhere, it stands enveloping all.
13.15: Shining through the functions of the senses yet without any sense, unattached yet supporting all, beyond the gunas yet experiencing them.
13.16: Outside and inside all beings, moving and unmoving, too subtle to be known, far away and yet near.
13.17: Undivided yet appearing divided among beings, it is the sustainer, the devourer and the creator.
13.18: The light of lights, said to be beyond darkness — knowledge, the object of knowledge and the goal of knowledge, seated in the hearts of all.
13.19: Thus the field, knowledge and the object of knowledge have been briefly described; My devotee, understanding this, enters My being.
13.20: Know that nature and spirit are both beginningless; modifications and qualities arise from nature.
13.21: Nature is the cause of body and organs; spirit is said to be the cause of the experience of pleasure and pain.
13.22: Spirit seated in nature experiences the qualities born of nature; attachment to those qualities causes birth in good and evil wombs.
13.23: The supreme spirit in this body is called the witness, the consenter, the supporter, the experiencer, the great Lord, the supreme Self.
13.24: One who thus knows spirit and nature with its qualities is not born again, whatever their condition of life.
13.25: Some see the Self in the self by meditation, others by the path of knowledge, others by the path of works.
13.26: Others, not knowing this, worship as they have heard from others; they too cross beyond death, devoted to what they have heard.
13.27: Whatever being is born, moving or unmoving, know it to arise from the union of the field and the knower of the field.
13.28: One who sees the supreme Lord dwelling equally in all beings, imperishable among the perishing, truly sees.
13.29: Seeing the same Lord everywhere, one does not injure the Self by the self, and so reaches the highest goal.
13.30: One who sees that all actions are performed by nature alone, and that the Self is not the doer, truly sees.
13.31: When one perceives the separate existence of beings resting in the One and spreading out from it, one attains Brahman.
13.32: Being beginningless and without qualities, this imperishable supreme Self neither acts nor is tainted, though dwelling in the body.
13.33: As all-pervading space is not tainted because of its subtlety, so the Self seated everywhere in the body is not tainted.
13.34: As one sun illumines this whole world, so the Lord of the field illumines the whole field.
13.35: Those who see with the eye of knowledge the difference between the field and its knower, and the liberation of beings from nature, reach the Supreme.
